# Claude Code Ultimate Guide

> The most comprehensive documentation for Claude Code CLI by Anthropic. Covers beginner to advanced: hooks, skills, agents, MCP servers, context engineering, memory systems, multi-agent orchestration, and production patterns.

Guide version 3.44.1, tracking Claude Code up to v2.1.310 (October 2026).

## What is covered

- Getting started: installation, CLAUDE.md setup, vocabulary, first session, 7-module learning path (8-11h)
- Concept distinctions: guide/core/ai-concept-boundaries.md compares context/window/memory, model/product/harness, assistant/workflow/agent, tool/MCP, instructions/access controls, evaluation/production evidence, and architecture/size/modality/task labels; seven original scenario checks, with attributed selective adaptation from Lexigraph (CC BY 4.0). Source limits: docs/resource-evaluations/lexigraph-ai-lexicon.md.
- Executable learning: installable learning-path skill with prerequisite gates, local evidence, scheduled reviews, and a tested seven-module companion project
- Context window management: 1M-token context on Sonnet 5, Opus 5.5, and Fable 5.1, context rot, /compact and /clear thresholds, auto-compact
- Context engineering: managing what the model sees, when and in what shape; token audit workflow, compression tools, ejection discipline, maturity model
- Memory systems: native stack (CLAUDE.md levels, auto memory, auto dream, agent frontmatter), cross-session tools (claude-mem, agentmemory, ICM, Kairn, OpenMemory), team sharing, file-based experience playbooks, memory poisoning risks
- Hook system: all 33 hook events with matchers, input schemas, exit-code-2 behavior and decision-control formats; blocking vs non-blocking
- Event ingestion and safe delegation: Monitor command/WebSocket sources, plugin monitors, MCP Channels, Routines GitHub triggers, and a read-only-first Codex workflow
- Slash commands: full categorized table of the ~100 built-in commands with aliases, mirroring the official reference at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands (the source of truth), plus removed and renamed commands
- Skills and slash commands: current SKILL.md frontmatter, description-based discovery, progressive disclosure, personal/project/vendor/marketplace ownership scopes, security versus maintenance boundaries, with/without-skill eval evidence, /skill-doctor, lifecycle and retirement, and the judgment-versus-harness decision
- Current product surfaces: Computer Use, plugin packaging and recommendation hints, Claude apps gateway, artifact publishing
- Agents: subagent frontmatter, delegation, agent teams, agent evaluation metrics, harness engineering
- AI design patterns: guide/core/ai-design-patterns.md maps 21 classic patterns (GoF, enterprise integration, distributed systems) to the closest Claude Code mechanism, states where each analogy breaks, and adds 8 agent-native patterns and 10 anti-patterns; each card links related workflows, templates, the author's tools and articles. Dataset: machine-readable/ai-design-patterns.json. A work in progress, not a reference.
- Agent harnesses: model-harness pair evidence, explicit loop and graph contracts, judgment allocation, durable execution, reviewer-independence tests, four operating layers plus an outer optimizer layer, a pinned 160-project source directory plus 33 guide supplements, 42 strict runtimes, 16 adjacent control planes, a research meta-harness table, a test-drive protocol, and DeepSeek Harness, Liza, and Multica profiles
- Multi-agent orchestration: parallel agents, hub-and-spoke coordinators, dynamic workflows (JavaScript-orchestrated pipelines, `ultracode`), agentic software factories, AI executive agents (virtual C-suites and board simulators applying the persona/agent pattern to named business roles)
- MCP server integration: setup, custom servers, validated community server catalog, MCP vs CLI vs Skills trade-offs, advanced tool design
- Guide MCP product reference: guide/ecosystem/claude-code-guide-mcp.md covers client installation, published versus candidate capabilities, architecture, privacy, offline behavior, troubleshooting, and dated npm/GSC/GA4 metrics
- Security and permission model: .claude/settings.json, permission rules, sandbox isolation, threat database, data privacy and retention, enterprise governance (guardrail tiers, MCP approval workflow, audit trails)
- CI/CD and code review: GitHub Actions patterns, the Code Review feature (Teams/Enterprise), multi-provider review pipelines
- Verification methods: bounded Best-of-N selection, independent review limits, permitted and rejected control cases, frozen evaluation criteria, cost per accepted task, executable checks, and TESTING.md proof records
- Frugal harnesses: distinguish repeated input billing from session loading, price generated notes against cached prefixes, append working-state snapshots after stable context, and scale plans and handoffs to task needs; Boucard attribution and evidence limits in docs/resource-evaluations/boucard-frugal-agent-harnesses.md
- Lean and AI flow: an explicitly bounded analogy to Toyota Just-in-Time and jidoka for review-capacity admission, queue measurement, stopping new authoring and testing recurring-defect controls; no measured software-team gain claimed
- Lean software engineering and methods: guide/core/methodologies.md compares BMAD, SDD, TDD, BDD and agent workflows against demand, WIP, built-in quality, revisable plans and recurring failures; includes Kanban flow metrics and evidence-limited project examples; gstack and Matt Pocock skill packs are assessed as optional controls, not measured Lean outcomes
- Ops and cost: AI FinOps section (cost regimes, lever map, and a dated, source-checked LLM market snapshot of API prices and subscription quotas), observability and session forensics, API gateway for enterprise cost control (LiteLLM, Portkey), AI unit economics, subscription strategy at team scale (Claude, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, Cursor, Mistral, governed API traffic, and self-hosted inference), team metrics (DORA, SPACE, agentic metrics)
- Mistral Large 4: October 6, 2026 source evaluation at docs/resource-evaluations/mistral-large-4.md; ecosystem API candidate, promotional versus original pricing, independent benchmark conditions, regional processing, specification discrepancies, and planned weights without a tested Claude Code or self-hosted integration
- Team knowledge infrastructure: 3-tier framework (Markdown vault, MCP connectors, RAG at scale), Code+Cowork bridge, Atlassian/Notion/GitBook MCP, Onyx/LlamaCloud/Ragie
- Adoption: L0-L5 maturity scale, the J-curve, empirical data (METR RCT, DeputyDev cohort), roles in AI-assisted teams
- Practitioner insights: condensed findings from IFTTD podcast episodes, Devoxx, ByteByteGo, Stanford Online, plus 150+ scored external resource evaluations
- Production templates: ready-to-use CLAUDE.md, rules, hooks, agents, skills, commands, quizzes, GitHub Actions workflows
- AI-assisted open source contributions: project policy, reproduction, author comprehension, evidence packets and follow-up; shared review-capacity admission and learning worksheets

- Agentic pentesting: guide/security/agentic-pentesting.md compares DarkMoon and Strix, exploit evidence, model data exposure, and evaluation requirements; source inspection and bounded local checks, no shared performance benchmark

- Harness control cases: Walkinglabs and AutoHarness evaluations distinguish structural scores, test coverage, activation and observed effects. The local review-control-demo.py has 13 tests with a simulated destination, not a live merge gate.
- WikiSkill: persistent proposal history, revisable wiki patterns, strict skill validation and executor-specific transfer. Full skill injection leaves routing untested; production gains are unmeasured. See docs/resource-evaluations/wikiskill-persistent-skill-evolution.md.
- Human supervision: comprehension, independent judgment, usable evidence, attention and recovery exercises; proposed practices without a local human trial. Three infographic topics are available in English and French.

- Architect-engineer handoffs: versioned self-contained contracts, ADRs, separate task/run/decision state, live-state reconciliation on resume, and review feedback. See guide/workflows/dual-instance-planning.md; role separation has no guaranteed cost or quality benefit, and Honkonen's eng CLI is custom tooling.
- Harness improvement: recoverable local quality requirements, semantic ownership, MLD observations before memory promotion, isolated curation candidates and versioned publication, worker requalification and four clocks. Selectively adapted from lopopolo/harness-engineering, an anthology rather than a runtime; no local gains measured.

## Machine-readable entry points

- machine-readable/reference.yaml: full index with file paths, anchors and line numbers into the guide
- machine-readable/claude-code-releases.yaml: condensed Claude Code release history, breaking changes, milestones
- machine-readable/cowork-reference.yaml: index for Claude Cowork (dedicated repo, non-dev audience)
- machine-readable/agentsec-security-feed.v1.json: AgentSec versions, detector coverage, security counters, and reviewed incident fiches consumed by the landing
- machine-readable/agent-harnesses.json: normalized Agent Harness Map with evidence states, official project URLs, and dated repository metadata
- machine-readable/mcp-product.json, mcp-stats.json, and mcp-dashboard.json: generated runtime contract plus dated package and aggregate page metrics with explicit availability and methodology boundaries
- machine-readable/translations.json: canonical, maintained, and community translation status with source checksums, versions, dates, and coverage
- machine-readable/distribution-channels.yaml: attributed publication channels, asset states, dates, and 30-day outcome fields
